approachQuestion.prompt:
A controller receives a nonnegative unsigned W-bit word x. Return a W-bit word that has exactly one set bit: the bit at the lowest position where x has a set bit. If x is zero, return zero. Bit positions are numbered from 0 at the least significant end.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 64; 0 <= x <= 2^W - 1. The result is an unsigned W-bit word. Arithmetic on words is defined modulo 2^W, and bitwise operations act on exactly W bits. A word operation takes constant time.

Example 1: W=8, x=44 (00101100₂) -> 4 (00000100₂).
Example 2 (edge case): W=8, x=0 -> 0.
Example 3 (top bit): W=5, x=16 (10000₂) -> 16 (10000₂).
constraints: Words are unsigned and exactly W bits; addition and negation wrap modulo 2^W. No signed right shift is used or needed.
A word-level bitwise operation or modular arithmetic operation takes constant time; inspecting one bit at a time counts as one operation per inspected position.
The output is one W-bit word; the input word and output are not auxiliary storage.

options.text: Compute x AND its modular negation (0 - x modulo 2^W), and return that word.
options.feedback: For a nonzero word, the low set bit is the only set bit shared by x and its modular negation; for zero, the result remains zero.

options.text: Test bit positions 0 through W-1 in order and return a word with only the first set position enabled; return zero if none is set.
options.feedback: This is correct for every allowed width and value, but examines positions individually instead of using one word-level operation to isolate the boundary bit.

options.text: Compute y = x AND (x - 1), then return x XOR y.
options.feedback: Subtracting one clears the lowest set bit and sets only lower zero positions; XOR with the original leaves exactly the removed lowest bit. This is equally optimal.

options.text: Count the zero bits from position 0 until the first set bit and return that count as an integer.
options.feedback: The required output is a word with only that bit set, not its position. For W=8 and x=44, this returns 2 instead of 4.

feedback.reason: Unsigned modular negation preserves the lowest one bit and complements higher contributions so AND isolates it.
details: Treat subtraction and negation as unsigned W-bit modular operations. For x = 0, modular negation is zero. Otherwise, below the lowest set bit all bits of x are zero; the modular negation carries through those positions, agrees at that bit, and differs above it. AND therefore preserves exactly that lowest set bit. The equivalent x AND (x - 1), followed by XOR with x, also returns the cleared bit.

Unsigned modular negation preserves the lowest one bit and complements higher contributions so AND isolates it. Clearing that bit with x AND (x-1) is a different operation. Zero must still produce zero.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For isolate-lowest-set-bit, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair in the stated word-RAM model. W is the word width. Exclude the input word and returned word.
constraints: Words are unsigned and exactly W bits; addition and negation wrap modulo 2^W. No signed right shift is used or needed.
A word-level bitwise operation or modular arithmetic operation takes constant time; inspecting one bit at a time counts as one operation per inspected position.

options.text: O(1) word operations, O(1) auxiliary words

feedback.reason: A fixed number of W-bit operations needs no bit-position scan.
details: The fixed method uses a fixed number of word-level arithmetic and bitwise operations regardless of W. It keeps only a fixed number of words and has no loop or recursion.
A constant number of word operations computes the result directly; the required output is one word and is excluded from auxiliary storage.
Only a fixed number of W-bit temporary words are used, independent of W. There is no per-bit table or call stack.
Unsigned W-bit words; negation and subtraction wrap modulo 2^W. The model defines each word-level operation as O(1); it does not rely on signed overflow or language-specific shift behavior.
Word-RAM: one input word and one output word are excluded; a fixed number of temporary words is O(1) auxiliary space. The bit-by-bit alternative takes O(W) time but O(1) auxiliary words.
“O(W) time, O(1) auxiliary words”: This describes checking positions one at a time, not the fixed word-level method.
“O(1) time, O(W) auxiliary words”: The fixed method allocates no array or other width-proportional storage.
“O(W) time, O(W) auxiliary words”: Neither the time nor storage matches the fixed word-level method.
